title: Redux Review Quiz
description: Review the small examples from this Redux course. Take your time and read the reason given for each answer.

questions.question: What does dispatch send to the store?
questions.explanation: A store keeps state. An action is a small message saying what happened, such as one more book being read.

questions.question: What forms the generated action type here?
options: The slice name and reducer name
questions.explanation: A slice groups one part of state with the reducers that change it. Its name also forms the start of generated action types.

questions.question: What is action.payload in this call?
questions.explanation: An action payload carries the information needed for a change. A reducer can use that value to choose the next state.

questions.question: How does a number-state reducer replace its value?
options: By changing a hidden field on the number
questions.explanation: When a slice state is a number or string, its reducer returns the next value. A primitive cannot be changed like a draft object field.

questions.question: Does this reducer change the original before object?
options: No, Toolkit produces a next state
Yes, all old state is overwritten
questions.explanation: Redux Toolkit uses Immer inside createSlice reducers. It records changes to a draft and makes a safe next state.

questions.question: What should each book have for stable identification?
questions.explanation: A list reducer can add a record with a stable id. The payload supplies the record to add.

questions.question: What should a selector do?
options: Read state and return a useful result
questions.explanation: A selector is a function that reads state and returns the part a caller needs. It keeps state lookup rules in one place.

questions.question: Where is the theme stored?
questions.explanation: A store can hold several slices under different keys. Each slice still handles its own part of the state.

questions.question: What does Provider make available?
options: The Redux store to descendant components
A database password to every visitor
questions.explanation: React Redux Provider makes one store available to components under it. Hooks can then read from that store.

questions.question: Which hook sends actions?
questions.explanation: useSelector reads a store value for a component. useDispatch gives the component a way to send actions.

questions.question: Which action carries a successful returned value?
questions.explanation: An async thunk creates pending, fulfilled and rejected actions for a promise. A reducer can use these to show task progress.

questions.question: Why keep reducers predictable?
options: It makes all network requests instant
It makes changes easier to test and understand
questions.explanation: Reducers should be predictable: the same state and action should produce the same result. Create outside facts before sending the action.
